title: Affine sections turn a scheme devissage chain into an algebra devissage
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a finite type homomorphism of commutative rings, $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime with inverse image $\mathfrak p\subset R$, and $N$ a finite $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Put $B=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $\widetilde N$ be the associated quasi-coherent module of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Suppose a pointed affine devissage chain of $\widetilde N/X/B$ at the point $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$ is given [def-trf-pointed-scheme-devissage-data]. Write $A_j=\Gamma(Z_j,\mathcal O_{Z_j})$, $C_j=\Gamma(Y_j,\mathcal O_{Y_j})$, and $M_j=\Gamma(Z_j,\mathcal G_j)$. Taking affine global sections of its ring maps, module isomorphisms and $\alpha_j$ gives a complete algebra devissage of $N/S/R$ over $\mathfrak p$ in [def-trf-complete-algebra-devissage], with the same length and ranks, $B_j=C_j$, and $\alpha_j:C_j^{\oplus r_j}\to M_j$. In particular $\mathfrak p C_j$ is prime and the residue-field map of this $\alpha_j$ is an isomorphism. The length-zero case gives the empty algebra devissage. No relative-dimension/support equalities beyond those in the auxiliary chain definition are needed for this implication.

source.place: Tags 05I0 (remark-same-notion), first assertion, and 05HX (definition-complete-devissage-algebra): affine sections of the scheme conditions after forgetting pointing and support-dimension equalities.

proof.text: Assume first that the chain has positive length $n$. Set $B_j=C_j$ and retain its ranks $r_j$. All schemes in the chain are affine by [def-trf-pointed-scheme-devissage-data]. The contravariant affine-spectrum dictionary gives $R$-algebra maps $S\to A_1$, $C_j\to A_j$, and $C_j\to A_{j+1}$, with the required scalar compatibilities because the scheme maps are over $\operatorname{Spec}R$. For $i_1$ and $i_{j+1}$, the affine closed-immersion criterion makes the first and third maps surjective. They are of finite presentation by the affine-opens finite-presentation lemma, since these immersions are of finite presentation and hence locally of finite presentation. Finiteness of $\pi_j$ gives finiteness of $A_j$ over $C_j$ directly from [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The affine finite-type criterion applied to $\mathcal G_j$ makes $M_j$ finite over $A_j$. Finally $\operatorname{Spec}C_j\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is the given smooth morphism with geometrically irreducible fibres.

source.place: Tag 05I0 (remark-same-notion), first assertion; Tag 05HX (definition-complete-devissage-algebra), conditions (1)--(4); Morphisms Tags 01QO and 01TQ; Properties Tag 01PB.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal H_j=\pi_{j,*}\mathcal G_j$. The finite map $\pi_j$ is affine by definition, so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] gives that $\mathcal H_j$ is quasi-coherent. The pushforward global-sections identification is the identity on elements and identifies $\Gamma(Y_j,\mathcal H_j)$ with $M_j$ carrying the restricted $C_j$-action. Under [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], $\mathcal H_j\cong\widetilde{M_j}$ and $\mathcal O_{Y_j}^{\oplus r_j}\cong\widetilde{C_j^{\oplus r_j}}$; the latter also follows from preservation of finite direct sums there. Thus global sections of the given $\alpha_j$ define a $C_j$-linear map $a_j:C_j^{\oplus r_j}\to M_j$, and the sheaf map is precisely $\widetilde{a_j}$ under these identifications, by the natural Hom bijection in that adjunction.

source.place: Tags 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions), 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback), part (2), and 01IB (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent); Cohomology of Schemes Tag 02KG (lemma-affine-base-change), quasi-coherence assertion; flat.tex Tag 05I0.

proof.text: For $j<n$, put $\mathcal Q_j=\operatorname{coker}(\alpha_j)$. Both source and target of $\alpha_j$ are quasi-coherent by the preceding step, so the affine cokernel formula of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] gives $\Gamma(Y_j,\mathcal Q_j)\cong\operatorname{coker}(a_j)$, using the quotient by the image of this very section map. The chain provides $i_{j+1,*}\mathcal G_{j+1}\cong\mathcal Q_j$. Its global sections and the pushforward section formula therefore give $\operatorname{coker}(a_j)\cong M_{j+1}$ over $C_j$, with action through $C_j\to A_{j+1}$. Similarly the first sheaf isomorphism $i_{1,*}\mathcal G_1\cong\widetilde N$ yields $M_1\cong N$ over $S$, since the tilde adjunction identifies $\Gamma(X,\widetilde N)$ with $N$. At the final index the same cokernel formula and $\mathcal Q_n=0$ give $\operatorname{coker}(a_n)=0$.

source.place: Tags 01IC (lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent), 01IB (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent), 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), part (2), and 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback), part (2); flat.tex Tag 05HH, conditions (3)--(4).

proof.text: Fix an index $j$ and abbreviate $C=C_j$. The affine fibre-product formula identifies $(Y_j)_b$ with $\operatorname{Spec}D$, where $D=C\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and its projection to $Y_j$ is induced by $c\mapsto c\otimes1$. Smoothness gives geometrically reduced fibres by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]; geometric irreducibility of the given fibre implies irreducibility and nonemptiness over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ itself. Consequently this fibre is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme], and its affine coordinate ring $D$ is a nonzero domain. This uses no support-dimension equality.

source.place: Tag 05I0 (remark-same-notion), generic-fibre translation in condition (7) of 05HX; Schemes Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); Varieties Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal); Properties Tag 01ON (lemma-characterize-integral).

proof.text: The smooth affine dictionary and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat] imply that $C$ is flat over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-quotient-flat], $E=C/\mathfrak p C$ is flat over the domain $R/\mathfrak p$. By [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain], multiplication by any nonzero element of $R/\mathfrak p$ on $E$ is injective. The fibre-ring formula in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] identifies $D$ with the localization of $E$ at those nonzero elements. The map $E\to D$ is injective: an element in its kernel is killed by one of these elements, and torsion-freeness makes it zero. Since $D$ is a nonzero domain and is a localization of $E$, $E$ is nonzero and has no zero divisors. Thus $P=\mathfrak p C$ is prime. The generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}D$ is $(0)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], and its image in $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is exactly $P$, the kernel of $C\to E\hookrightarrow D$. Hence the chain's $\xi_j$ maps to the prime $\mathfrak p C_j$.

source.place: Tag 05I0 and Tag 05HX condition (7); Algebra Tag 00TA (lemma-smooth-syntomic), Tag 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change); Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves). The injection into the localized domain is written out.

proof.text: At $P=\mathfrak p C_j$, the tilde stalk formula identifies the stalk map of $\widetilde{a_j}$ with $(a_j)_P:(C_j)_P^{\oplus r_j}\to(M_j)_P$. Indeed on germs of global sections it sends $m/1$ to $a_j(m)/1$, and $C_j$-linearity then determines its values on all fractions. Tensoring with $\kappa(P)$ identifies the resulting map with $a_j\otimes_{C_j}\kappa(P)$. Explicitly, the tensor identification sends $(m/s)\otimes\lambda$ to $m\otimes\bar s^{-1}\lambda$ and its inverse sends $m\otimes\lambda$ to $(m/1)\otimes\lambda$; $s\notin P$ makes $\bar s$ invertible. These formulas commute with $a_j$ and identify the source with $\kappa(P)^{\oplus r_j}$ coordinatewise, including $r_j=0$. Thus the chain's stipulated residue-field isomorphism at $\xi_j$, now identified with $P$, is exactly the isomorphism $\kappa(P)^{\oplus r_j}\to M_j\otimes_{C_j}\kappa(P)$ required by the algebra definition.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), parts (6)--(7), and Tag 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions); flat.tex Tags 05HH condition (2) and 05HX condition (7).

proof.text: Use $a_j$ as the algebraic $\alpha_j$. Step 1 supplies all the algebra maps, finiteness, smoothness and geometric irreducibility. Steps 2--3 supply their scalar actions and the initial, successive and final module identifications. Steps 4--6 supply primality of $\mathfrak p C_j$ and the required residue-field isomorphisms. These are precisely all the clauses of [def-trf-complete-algebra-devissage], with the same indices and ranks. If instead $n=0$, the scheme-chain definition requires $\widetilde N=0$; the unit isomorphism $N\cong\Gamma(X,\widetilde N)$ gives $N=0$, so the algebra definition permits the empty list. The pointing, purely transcendental residue extensions, and relative dimensions impose no further condition on this conclusion.
